identityReview: Edmundo González Urrutia, born 29 August 1949 in La Victoria, Venezuelan former diplomat and 2024 main opposition presidential candidate. Not Felipe González, whose biography shares the event page, or Mexican writer Edmundo González Llaca. Recognition as elected president is separate from actually exercising state power; November 2026 reporting identifies Delcy Rodríguez’s acting government. Shared Sakharov recognition does not transfer another individual’s awards or offices to him.
lifeStatusEvidence: Euronews reports a new joint Madrid Declaration by González and Machado on 5 November 2026, supporting continued public political activity. Cotejo’s 17 November publication, researched through 15 November, describes continued exile and rebuts a recirculated old return interview; it is not treated as a new interview or live appearance on publication day. No unsupported current medical status or exact current physical location is asserted.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read the event organiser’s campaign-derived biography; relevant profile section in the Rosario/KAS report; CNN’s syndicated candidacy report; Carter Center’s initial statement and relevant final-report sections; European Parliament’s accessible award announcement and ceremony account; Europa Press’s asylum report; and the November Euronews, Cotejo and La Prensa de Lara reporting. Read Commons history, the original Flickr description and its linked Creative Commons deed.
corrections: Read the Nueva Economía Fórum event biography, explicitly attributed to edmundopresidente.com. It supports birth on 29 August 1949 in La Victoria, UCV undergraduate study, subsequent master’s study, diplomatic postings and confirmation as unity candidate on 19 April 2024. This is a campaign-derived biography reproduced by an event organiser, not an independently audited personnel or university record. Its 1991–1994 Algeria and 1993–1998 foreign-ministry ranges differ from the Rosario profile; retain the existence of those roles without fixing disputed endpoints. The scheduled 23 December event is not used as proof of attendance. The page also contains Felipe González’s biography, whose offices and books must not be assigned to Edmundo.

Read the Edmundo profile section on printed page 14 of RADAR Colombia Venezuela’s June 2024 report, not the entire PDF. It identifies an international-studies education at UCV and an American University international-relations master’s in 1981. Both this profile and the event biography record service in Argentina in 1999–2002. Their early Algeria and ministry dates differ, so the display notes the discrepancy. Mercosur-related negotiation is not proof of completed accession during his ambassadorship. Academic and writing activity is not a university presidency or professorial rank. Pre-election polling figures elsewhere in the document are not election results.

Read CNN en Español’s report syndicated by KESQ, carrying an original 19 April timestamp and a 20 April publication field. The decision occurred on Friday 19 April. It confirms existing provisional registration before the opposition’s unity decision, Machado’s exclusion, Yoris’s inability to register, and support from Rosales. Do not call 19 April the first registration or claim that Machado and Yoris faced identical legal procedures. Reported party reactions are attributed statements, not independent electoral certification.

Read the final Carter Center report’s candidate-registration discussion and results-form analysis on printed pages 35–36, not all of the report or its annexes. The analysis concerns published actas covering 81.7% of polling stations; 67.1% for González and 30.4% for Maduro are from that dataset, not a complete CNE nationwide breakdown. The Center checked security features and a random transcription sample, and concluded the announced Maduro victory was statistically impossible even with extreme assumptions about missing stations. This is its documented conclusion, not a claim that this project recounted original ballots. The text and table differ by one in the tally-sheet count, and the extracted table has malformed numeric fields; omit those precise counts rather than reproduce them. The report’s later analysis must not be backdated to its 30 July initial statement.

Read the Carter Center’s 30 July 2024 statement. It could not verify or corroborate the CNE-announced result and found the election failed international standards of electoral integrity. It describes a limited observation mission of 17 experts and observers, not observation of every polling station. Preserve the distinction between this early assessment and later analysis of opposition-published tally sheets; neither makes the electoral process itself free and fair.

Read the European Parliament’s 24 October 2024 joint Sakharov award announcement and its account of the 19 September resolution recognising González. Recognition is by Parliament, not automatically by each EU member-state government, the European Council or the UN. Award selection and the December presentation are separate dates. Its shorthand claim of asylum granted on 7 September is qualified by the Spanish minister’s later December announcement of approved status; the dossier separates September refuge/arrival and the December public confirmation. Historic descriptions of Maduro’s government are not carried forward as current November 2026 officeholding.

Read the European Parliament’s 17 December 2024 ceremony release. González received the joint Sakharov Prize in Strasbourg; Machado was represented there by her daughter Ana Corina Sosa and spoke remotely. Do not describe both laureates as physically present or confuse their shared 2024 Sakharov award with another award to Machado. Parliament’s reporting also corroborates the September recognition and departure following an arrest warrant. The linked resolution and September news release produced a JavaScript challenge rather than readable substantive text; the dossier relies on the accessible October and December institutional reports, not a claim to have inspected the resolution itself. No ceremony video was watched.

Read Europa Press’s 20 December 2024 report of Albares’s announcement and meeting with González. The minister said asylum had already been granted, with notification to follow; 20 December is therefore the public announcement date, not a verified date on the administrative decision. The report places arrival in Spain on 8 September. It does not establish an earlier September date for completed formal approval. Public intentions to return on 10 January were prospective and do not prove that a return or inauguration occurred.

Read Euronews’s 5 November 2026 report of the Madrid Declaration jointly signed by Machado and González. This recent public statement supports continuing political activity, but does not establish that both physically attended the summit or signed together in Madrid. It identifies Delcy Rodríguez’s acting government separately from the opposition and reports support for renewed judicial/electoral institutions and future elections. The timetable and proposed 2030 summit venue are proposals, not completed actions. Claims in the declaration about a US route are attributed within that document, not independently verified binding US policy or a legally fixed election date.

Read Cotejo.info’s fact check published 17 November 2026, with its investigation explicitly current through 15 November. It traces a recirculated return announcement to an El País interview of 9 December 2024 and says the planned January 2025 assumption of office did not occur. It reports continued exile in Spain and no completed return by its research cutoff. The article’s later publication date is not a new interview, live appearance or independent evidence of a 17 November location. No underlying video or X post was watched or independently authenticated; the fact-check’s textual findings are attributed, and do not replace checking newer actual travel before publication.

Read La Prensa de Lara’s 6 November 2026 fact check. It identifies an Ecuadorian Order of Merit ceremony on 28 January 2025 as the source of a falsely labelled presidential-inauguration clip. Receiving a foreign honour is not taking office in Venezuela. The report also recounts his 8 September 2024 arrival at Torrejón following an arrest warrant; a warrant is not a conviction. Its wording equating the barriers facing Machado and Yoris is overbroad, so candidacy uses the more precise CNN and Carter descriptions. No embedded video or linked Ecuadorian original report was inspected.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not native-language human certification. No university transcript, original electoral-ballot recount, full final-report or annex audit, original asylum decision, blocked parliamentary text, audiovisual or image-pixel review. Preserve contested dates, institutional scope of recognition, proposal versus completed event, and source publication date versus activity date. Refresh political officeholding and travel before publication.

portraitReview.unresolved: Read Commons metadata/history and the linked Peruvian foreign-ministry Flickr page. Candidate is 670×838. Commons lists 19 November 2025 as its date, whereas Flickr says taken 28 January 2025 and uploaded 7 February 2025; preserve the conflict pending comparison with original image and event provenance. LLs uploaded to Commons on 15 March 2026 and Leoboudv confirmed the Flickr licence on 17 March. These are uploader/reviewer roles, not photographer identities; the generic own-work upload comment does not override the explicit ministry attribution. Flickr’s rights link resolves directly to CC BY-SA 2.0, matching Commons. No named photographer or crop editor is verified. Download on 18 November failed with curl 22, HTTP 403 and reported HTTP 000; the referenced collection cache is absent. Image bytes, identity, colour, crop suitability and the relationship to the Flickr original remain visually unverified.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages checked against Chinese and English. Preserve polling-station coverage and the denominator of vote percentages; early inability to verify versus later analysis; provisional registration versus April unity endorsement; differing barriers for Machado and Yoris; September arrival versus December public asylum announcement; award announcement versus presentation and Machado’s representation; parliamentary recognition versus each government’s position and actual power transfer; arrest warrant versus conviction; proposed elections versus completed events; and early diplomatic service versus completed Mercosur accession.
